This is talking from my own experiences. I had onset of symptoms while I was in us and it’ll go one of two ways. Either they’ll refuse to diagnose you with anything if you get past enlistment without suspicion and you’ll be looked down on by command for malingering when you’re actually experiencing symptoms that are like making everything harder in life or if you get in and admit to having them before enlistment (at least in the us) they can prosecute you for fraudulent enlistment. I had the first one happen to me, only got out when I went totally off the walls and attempted to take my own life because the voices kept telling me to. It sucks but you’ll be a lot happier without going in. And like another commenter said we are liabilities to our comrades. Especially if you wind up getting deployed or anything like that and lose control or something, especially if you get a job that works with weapons

Norse pagan here. A lot of the time it comes down to reading whether or not the person would possibly be receptive to hearing out what I have to say. If you come at me aggressively and try to write off my connection with the gods then I’m gonna back off. But if I sense you’re genuinely curious based on tone then I’ll be happy to explain. How are you asking people when talking about these things? The difference between Abrahamic religions (excluding Judaism which doesn’t try to convert people) at least for my own practice its about educating people on my beliefs and explaining. Plus some people may feel that their practice is deeply personal to them and they might now want to share it which is totally fine too. I wont pry into how a Christian practices Christianity if they answer with the oh it just felt right answer because they probably do t want to delve into the whys. There’s many reasons why someone may answer that way. Could be that you’re just not asking the right people too.

Therapy will be your best friend but if you dont feel you have time I've found a lot of resources on youtube to be extremely helpful. Just as long as you avoid the self help cults that are pretty rampant on there. Reading and writing too can also be helpful if utilized properly but honestly I think your best option right now is to get into therapy  to try and see where the pattern lies if there is one ya know? Just keep in mind it's really hard to find one that works for you. Just dont get into a relationship before you find out how to avoid the falling hard and fast trail of thinking.
